triage_context.environment: Internet-facing multi-tenant SaaS (apps/main); internal service-to-service (apps/rag). HTTP untrusted; authenticated tenant users semi-trusted; cross-tenant + financial integrity are key threats.
triage_context.scoring: derived HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW from preconditions x access
triage_context.votes_per_finding: 1 for MEDIUM+HIGH (dedicated adversarial verifier); LOWs triaged inline against exclusion rules

findings.title: Concurrent booking-cancel double-counts clawback in platform_revenue (settled-payout branch has no CAS gate)
findings.rationale: Settled-payout branch (route.ts:217-275) inserts a negative platform_revenue row with no CAS, no unique/ON-CONFLICT (confirmed absent in migration 20260525000000_money_columns.sql:67-77), and never advances payout_records.status off 'paid', so two concurrent cancels both insert. Stripe createReversal is idempotency-keyed (money moves once) but the ledger row is not. Pending branch IS guarded (#846); settled is not + untested.
findings.recommendation: Claim the payout row with a CAS (.update({status:'reversed'}).eq('id',payout.id).eq('status',payout.status).select('id') asserted to 1 via safeAwaitRowCount) before reversal+ledger insert; else 409. Or add a unique idempotency key on platform_revenue with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
preconditions: authenticated agent with bookings:cancel
two concurrent/duplicate cancel requests (double-click/retry/parallel)
booking commission 'received' with a settled payout

findings.title: Customer chat hard-limit is read-modify-write, not atomic
findings.rationale: enforceCustomerLimit reads current_count, computes nextCount=current+1, decides hard tier on the stale read, writes via plain UPDATE on (user_id,tenant_id) with no CAS/atomic increment (customer-limit.ts:104-111,139,248-250). resolve_customer_chat_caps only resolves caps, never increments. K concurrent requests at cap-1 all pass and call the paid model.
findings.recommendation: Atomic increment RPC (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET current_count=current_count+1 RETURNING current_count); decide cap against the returned value (consume-then-check). Mirror increment_tenant_ai_cost.
preconditions: authenticated customer at hard_cap-1
concurrent requests

findings.title: Anonymous chat limit check+increment non-atomic
findings.rationale: checkAnonLimit SELECT-gate then a separate read-then-write incrementAnonCounters (UPDATE branch has no CAS/row-count guard; PK only mitigates the fresh-zero INSERT race). No middleware/Redis/edge limiter. N parallel anon requests all pass and reach the paid Anthropic call, bypassing the free-tier signup wall.
findings.recommendation: Atomic ON CONFLICT increment RPC returning post-increment; reject when exceeding the cap (consume-then-check). Back anon limits with Redis.
preconditions: unauthenticated
N parallel requests on a fresh session/IP/fingerprint

findings.title: AI-cost hard gate reads 30s per-instance cache + fire-and-forget transition
findings.rationale: Hard refusal (call-wrapper.ts:301, mirrored stream-wrapper.ts:177, chat preflight 489) reads ai_cost_state from loadTenantSnapshot 30s Map cache; the 'hard' flip is dispatched void AFTER the call (364) → up-to-30s per-instance enforcement lag. increment_tenant_ai_cost only sums cents, no enforcement. D-091 #6.
findings.recommendation: Enforce the hard cap against fresh ledger state at call time (uncached read, or have the increment RPC return cumulative cents and reject on crossing) and await the hard-boundary transition; soft tiers may stay cached.
preconditions: tenant at/near the hard ceiling
burst of calls within the staleness window

findings.title: Unauthenticated unthrottled OTP-mint route enables identity binding
findings.rationale: prompt route has no session/permission/rate-limit; mints OTP keyed only by email, resets attempts:0 each call (otp-store.ts), verify binds email->caller's session identity via admin.updateUserById(...,email_confirm:true). Per-email cap defeated by regeneration; per-IP limiter only on verify (per-instance, IP-rotatable). Fresh code per mint keeps practical brute-force bounded → MEDIUM not HIGH.
findings.recommendation: Bind OTP to the authenticated session (key by auth_user_id), require a session in the prompt route, add per-IP + per-email regeneration caps to prompt, back limiters with Redis.
preconditions: attacker has own OAuth session
IP rotation for the per-IP verify limiter

findings.title: Anonymous chat streams raw DB error.message via SSE (two sinks)
findings.rationale: Anon-reachable. catch sink at 235-237 streams err.message (SupabaseMutationError embeds pgError.message via safe-mutation.ts:38); ALSO direct interpolation of createErr.message at line 460 on the conversation-create path. Every sibling chat route uses dbErrorResponse; this one doesn't. Schema/table/column disclosure to unauth callers.
findings.recommendation: Route the SSE error path through a dbErrorResponse-equivalent (generic message + server-logged ref); replace the line-460 interpolation with a generic token.
preconditions: unauthenticated request that trips a DB constraint/error

findings.title: SSRF via admin-stored RSS feed URL (full scheme+host control, follows redirects)
findings.rationale: fetchFeedItems fetches news_feeds.url; feeds POST validates only new URL() (no scheme allowlist, no link-local/metadata/RFC1918 block), default redirect:follow. Parsed item content persisted + surfaced (semi-blind exfil). Platform-admin-gated (assertPlatformAdminArea 'travel_news'); env marks stored-URL SSRF to metadata as untrusted/priv-esc. No SSRF guard helper exists. THREAT_MODEL T12.
findings.recommendation: https-only scheme allowlist; resolve host and block loopback/link-local/RFC1918/.internal (re-validate post-DNS); redirect:'manual' with per-hop re-validation; centralize as the T9/T12 SSRF guard.
preconditions: platform-admin (or service bearer) writes a news_feeds row
6-hourly cron or manual-refresh fires

findings.title: Public chat token ignores quote/itinerary status -> stale token loads customer PII
findings.rationale: resolvePublicToken returns status but the chat route never reads it (sibling quote/select enforces sent/viewed + #741 CAS). Token has no expiry/revocation column; resource status is the only kill-switch and it's ignored. resolveCustomerContext injects cruise/ship/sailing/cabin/price/agent_notes PII into the LLM prompt on a declined/expired/forwarded token.
findings.recommendation: Reject when the resource is not customer-viewable (quotes sent/viewed + valid_until; itineraries not archived) before any context load; test declined/expired/archived tokens are refused.
preconditions: possession of a forwarded/leaked but stale token

findings.title: source_url/image_url accept file://+internal; rendered in unguarded client sinks
findings.rationale: z.string().url() accepts file://+internal hosts (also approve/reference/itinerary/media-asset schemas). Persisted verbatim, returned at retrieve:210-211. RAG never fetches it server-side, but main app renders it: AssetLightbox.tsx:44 NO scheme check, MessageSources.tsx:55 NO scheme check (renderMessageContent gates http(s) on the chat path only). Internal http(s) fires a client-side GET. Reclassed client-side SSRF, not server-side.
findings.recommendation: Tighten the contract: scheme allowlist (http/https) + private-range host deny at ingest (single chokepoint), and/or enforce the http(s) gate at every render sink (AssetLightbox, MessageSources).
preconditions: write/admin ingest of a crafted URL
end user views the retrieved citation/asset

findings.title: Feedback rate-limit runs before HMAC; spoofable shared bucket + pre-auth Redis writes
findings.rationale: checkFeedbackRateLimit (60) runs before HMAC compare (71). Bucket key rl:feedback:${remote}:${secretHint}: remote=spoofable x-forwarded-for, secretHint=server constant. Unauth attacker setting XFF to the main app's (stable) egress IP shares + exhausts the legit caller's 120/min bucket -> real feedback 429'd before its HMAC is checked; every POST also does a pre-auth redis.incr. NOTE title 'fail-open' is a misnomer — it fails CLOSED in prod; the bug is auth-ordering.
findings.recommendation: Verify HMAC FIRST, then rate-limit only authenticated requests; drop the constant secretHint from the key; don't bucket on spoofable forwarded-for.
preconditions: knowledge of the main app's egress IP (stable/discoverable)

findings.title: Feedback webhook replayable to poison retrieval ranking (no ts/nonce/dedup)
findings.rationale: HMAC covers only the static body; no timestamp/nonce/replay-cache; feedback inserts N rows with no source_revision/dedup (sibling tenant-events/platform-settings have a monotonic guard). One captured signed request replays forever, crossing feedback_min_signal_count and inflating compute_feedback_factor's decay-weighted sum up to the ±clamp -> steers what the LLM retrieves. Clamp bounds it to MEDIUM.
findings.recommendation: Add a signed timestamp+skew window and a per-request nonce/jti in the Redis replay cache (or a dedup key on (message_id,chunk_id)), mirroring the source_revision pattern.
preconditions: capture one valid signed feedback request (on-path/log leak)

findings.title: Public-chat rate limit is per-instance in-memory
findings.rationale: Sole pre-LLM gate is a module-level Map (30/token/hr); no middleware/WAF/Redis. On Vercel it resets on cold start and is per-instance -> bypassable via fan-out, each allowed request = paid Anthropic + supervisor. Bounded per-tenant by the durable AI hard-cap (AiCostHardStateError ~70% budget) -> MEDIUM/LOW-MED. A durable DB limiter (customer_chat_counters) exists and isn't wired here.
findings.recommendation: Use the shared Redis limiter keyed by token AND source IP before the LLM call; keep the in-memory map as a fast path only.
preconditions: possession of one valid public token

findings.title: Office/PDF parsers decompress untrusted uploads before the output cap (zip-bomb)
findings.rationale: mammoth/exceljs/officeparser fully decompress OOXML ZIPs in memory; only input caps (50MB) and a 1MB OUTPUT cap applied AFTER extraction. ~50MB compressible OOXML expands to GBs (DEFLATE ~50-1000:1) -> OOMs the bounded serverless function before the cap runs. No ratio/streaming guard; no concurrency cap. Auth-gated, availability-only -> MEDIUM. The output-cap comment falsely claims to mitigate this. (Correction: the 10MB imports path is PDF-only, not a second OOXML surface.)
findings.recommendation: Enforce a decompressed-size/ratio budget during extraction (central-directory sizes or streaming unzip with per-entry+total caps) before/while parsing; or a hard memory/time budget treating OOM as failed; fix the misleading comment.
preconditions: authenticated tenant member with rag_submissions:create

findings.title: No size cap on ingest content (downgraded MED->LOW)
findings.rationale: Downgraded by verifier: the headline raw_content path queues to human approval (no spend until /approve); per-request cost is bounded by OpenAI's 8192-token cap (oversize 400s, no charge); sync-embed reference/itinerary routes are platform-admin-only. The real vector is request VOLUME (rate limit), which a .max() doesn't fix. Already tracked as THREAT_MODEL T9 partially_mitigated.
findings.recommendation: Optional hardening: bounded .max() on raw_content/text for fail-fast validation AND/OR a per-route/per-tenant ingest rate limit (the volumetric vector). Do not treat as MEDIUM.
preconditions: write-scoped or platform-admin service JWT
looped requests (volumetric)

findings.title: Raw DB error.message echoed to authenticated caller
findings.recommendation: Use dbErrorResponse; also rag/submit/batch:70, help/* db_error returns.

findings.title: Raw DB error.message echoed on batch insert failure
findings.recommendation: Use dbErrorResponse.

findings.title: Quote accepted transition has no source-state guard
findings.recommendation: CAS .in('status',['sent','draft']).select('id'); 409 on zero rows.

findings.title: line-item POST doesn't verify parent booking ownership
findings.recommendation: SELECT booking .eq('id',bookingId).eq('tenant_id',ctx.tenant_id) and 404 before insert (mirror #715).

findings.title: relationship POST doesn't verify contact ownership
findings.recommendation: SELECT both contacts via tenantClient; 404/400 if either missing before insert.

findings.title: quote_options lookup not tenant-scoped (single-layer)
findings.recommendation: Add .eq('tenant_id',quote.tenant_id) to the select and both updates.

findings.title: Unsubscribe HMAC tokens never expire
findings.recommendation: Stamp exp (mirror companion tokens); accept missing-exp for backward compat.

findings.title: Imported-commission gross uses float math, bypasses money.ts (dormant)
findings.recommendation: Use multiplyRate(BigInt(commissionable), toRate(rate.rate)) from @/lib/money.

findings.title: Two admin GET routes read cross-tenant via raw service-role without audit
findings.recommendation: Wrap both reads in withPlatformAdminAudit (admin_user_id:'service:bearer', reason).

findings.title: Proxy admin gate is a cookie shape-check (structural fragility)
findings.recommendation: Add a CI guard asserting every app/api/admin/**/route.ts references assertPlatformAdmin*/assertPlatformRole or the MAIN_APP_ADMIN_API_KEY compare.

findings.title: Zero-tolerance PII prefilter misses separator variants
findings.recommendation: Normalize (strip [\s.\-]) into a digits-only view and run Luhn/SSN structural checks; add dotted/unseparated fixtures.

findings.title: Primary vector path is DB-only single-layer (no JS re-filter)
findings.recommendation: Add the JS re-filter to vectorRows (drop scope==='tenant' && tenant_id!==ctx) matching the other paths.

findings.title: Service JWT verified without aud/iss binding
findings.recommendation: Add audience+issuer to SignJWT and jwtVerify.

findings.title: Destructive admin routes gate on identifier but not write scope
findings.recommendation: Add `if (ctx.scope !== 'write') return 403` to purge/demote/post-termination-mark/post-termination-review/set-authority-override; test a read-scoped admin token is rejected.

findings.title: Hand-rolled string timingSafeEqual with early length-return
findings.recommendation: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(provided),Buffer.from(expected)) like the sibling routes.

findings.title: Resend webhook has no dedup (operational, not attacker-triggerable)
findings.recommendation: Persist svix-id in a dedup table (atomic insert-or-409) before dispatch, mirroring Stripe.

findings.title: Gmail history pointer advanced after loop (operational)
findings.recommendation: Confirm processGmailInboundMessage idempotency per message_id; gate import.queued on tenant_id+message_id.

findings.title: Stripe error path deletes idempotency row before 500
findings.recommendation: Confirm every dispatch branch is replay-safe; consider keeping the errored row and gating reprocessing on outcome.

findings.title: Arithmetic regex on AI candidate responses (ReDoS unconfirmed)
findings.recommendation: Cap scanned length (slice 20000) + restructure the number token; add a bounded-time test.

findings.title: Tenant member can claim an un-claimed anon session (needs UUID)
findings.recommendation: Bind commit to the originating atc-anon-session cookie.

findings.title: CruiseMapper fetcher follows redirects, no internal-IP block (host operator-controlled)
findings.recommendation: Apply the same SSRF guard as F-ssrf-01 (scheme allowlist, internal-IP block, redirect:'manual').

findings.title: Commission state-machine CAS (FALSE POSITIVE)
findings.rationale: All production callers transition to the SAME terminal value 'waived'; no divergent concurrent writer exists, so last-writer-wins is a no-op. The real money race is the un-CAS'd payout branch = F-pay-01. A status CAS here is hardening (rule 13), not the fix.

findings.title: Retrieved content not untrusted-tagged (FALSE POSITIVE)
findings.rationale: Harm is realized only in the downstream LLM caller (main app); RAG is a retrieval API that never constructs a prompt. Contract already carries scope/source_type/authority. Rule 6 (prompt-injection input) + rule 13 (hardening-only).

findings.title: Storage path startsWith traversal (FALSE POSITIVE)
findings.rationale: Supabase Storage treats '..' as a literal key segment (flat S3-style keyspace), so '../' doesn't escape the tenant prefix. Object-storage traversal exclusion. One-line hardening still worthwhile: reject '..'.
